item.title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $f(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $\pi$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, \pi\times\chi)\overline{L(1/2, \chi)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{\chi\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Ghosh, Pratim Mitra

item.title: Ehrhart Polynomials of Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.
item.dc:creator: Max Aldrich, Daniel Gulbrandsen, Clara Keddy

item.title: On the Diophantine equation $X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Diophantine equation \[ X^2+p^m=p_1^{n_1}p_2^{n_2}, \] where $p,p_1,p_2$ are distinct odd primes. Using factorizations in quadratic fields, sharp bounds for linear forms in two $p$-adic logarithms, elementary methods, and known results on exponential Diophantine equations, we obtain explicit bounds for $m,n_1,n_2$, and consequently the finiteness of the number of solutions for fixed $p,p_1,p_2$.
item.dc:creator: Amir Ghadermarzi

item.title: CM Elliptic Analogue of the Coleman--Ihara Formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.21052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Soul\'{e} characters are Kummer characters constructed from cyclotomic units and also arising from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. The Coleman--Ihara formula describes the restrictions of these characters to the local Galois group at $p$ as products of the Coates--Wiles homomorphisms and Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-values at positive odd integers. In this paper, we prove an elliptic analogue of this formula for elliptic curves with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field $K$. We consider certain Kummer characters associated with elliptic units, which we call elliptic Soul\'{e} characters. These characters are elliptic counterparts of the classical Soul\'{e} characters and also arise from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental groups of once-punctured elliptic curves. For suitable pairs of positive integers $(i,j)$, we give an explicit description of their restrictions to the relevant local Galois groups as products of the two-variable Coates--Wiles homomorphisms introduced by Yager and the two-variable $p$-adic $L$-values of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Goto, Shun Ishii

item.title: A simpler proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros
item.description: arXiv:2610.21099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper simplifies the recent OpenAI proof that there are no Landau--Siegel zeros.
item.dc:creator: Bryce Kerr

item.title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.21169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The formal derivative of the reduced polynomial representative of a map on a binary finite field depends on the coordinates, although its differential uniformity does not. This matters for lifting permutations to Galois rings: a polynomial over a Galois ring of characteristic a power of two greater than two permutes the ring exactly when its reduction permutes the residue field and the derivative of the reduction has no zero there. We prove that for every odd $n\ge5$, every quadratic almost perfect nonlinear permutation $Q$ of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ admits invertible binary-linear maps $L$ and $A$ such that the derivative of the reduced representative of $L\circ Q\circ A$ has no zero and each of its nonempty fibres has exactly two elements. The range is exact: this fails for $n=3$, as computed earlier, and for even $n$ there are no such permutations. For $n\ge9$, a linearization and a projectively injective cofactor map reduce the problem to counting binary matrices: more than 5% of the invertible inputs $A$ succeed, more than half for $n\ge15$, without any classification. For $n=5,7$ we use two independent classifications and finite certificates. Consequently every such permutation is linearly equivalent to a counterexample to the reduced critical-point conjecture of Bartoli and St\u{a}nic\u{a} that lifts to permutation polynomials of optimal differential uniformity over every Galois ring with this residue field. For odd $n\ge9$ the existence proof is checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Explicit reduced APN permutations: ramification and optimal Galois-ring lifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.21178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $m\ge5$ be odd and $q=2^m$. For every odd $r$ with $3\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$ we give the reduced polynomial $P_{m,r}=\mathrm{red}((T_r^3)^{2^{m-2}})$, $T_r=\sum_{i<r}X^{2^i}$, explicitly: it has coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_2$ and exactly $3r-2$ terms, it is an APN permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$, and its formal derivative $1+X^{2^{r-2}}+X^{2^{m-2}}$ has no zero on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and is two-to-one. We determine the ramification of $P_{m,r}$ as a map of the projective line for all admissible $(m,r)$: there are $2^{m-r}$ finite ramification points, all wild, with index and different exponent $2^{r-2}$, all over the single finite branch value $1$. The $0/1$ lift of $P_{m,r}$ satisfies an identity in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ that evaluates it over every Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ with $m-1$ squarings, one general multiplication and $r+5$ additions or subtractions. For every quadratic optimal APN permutation $p$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ (in particular $P_{m,r}$), every $k\ge2$ and every coefficient lift $F$ of $p$ to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$, we determine the differential rows of $F$ exactly in the unit directions whose residue lies outside the kernel $\{0,\rho\}$ of the linear part of $p'$ (they are the residue rows of $p$; $\rho=1$ for $P_{m,r}$) and in the directions in $2^{k-1}\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)\setminus\{0\}$ (every nonzero entry equals $2q^{k-1}$). We also give a self-contained proof of the Li--Wang criterion for a Gold function plus a linearised polynomial, which explains why the inner map of $P_{m,r}$ is not a monomial, and record a two-word, two-layer transition that a simple linear layer forbids at the residue level.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Non-vanishing mod $p$ of derived Hecke algebras of multiplicative groups over number fields, II
item.description: arXiv:2610.21278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the derived Hecke action on the cohomology of an arithmetic manifold associated to the multiplicative group over a number field. Under mild assumptions, we prove that the derived Hecke action is non-vanishing modulo $p$ in every degree. Moreover, the total cohomology ring with $\mathbb F_p$-coefficients is a free graded module of rank one over the derived Hecke algebra, generated in degree zero.
item.dc:creator: Jaesung Kwon

item.title: Modularity criteria for multiple Eisenstein series
item.description: arXiv:2610.21291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give two criteria for a linear combination of multiple Eisenstein series of fixed weight to be a modular form, one in terms of its Fourier coefficients and one in terms of its $L$-function. The first criterion follows from an exact transformation formula under $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, which describes the modular defect of multiple Eisenstein series explicitly. The second criterion is a Hecke converse theorem for multiple Eisenstein series, which shows that the functional equation of the $L$-function alone already implies modularity.
item.dc:creator: Jinbo Yu

item.title: On the dimension conjecture for global Galois deformation rings in characteristic two
item.description: arXiv:2610.21298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes. Let $G_{K,S}$ be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic extension of $K$ unramified outside $S$. We prove two refined lower bounds for the Krull dimension of unrestricted global Galois deformation rings of continuous absolutely irreducible representations of $G_{K,S}$ over finite fields of characteristic $2$. As applications, we construct the first counterexamples to the dimension conjecture in every dimension $n\geq 2$ over every number field with a real prime. Over every totally real number field, these constructions also yield the first examples of such universal deformation rings that fail to be complete intersections. Furthermore, we propose a modified dimension conjecture for $K=\mathbb{Q}$ and $n=2$.
item.dc:creator: Yufan Luo

item.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
item.description: arXiv:2610.21488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $\delta_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We prove the smoothness of $\delta_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional.
item.dc:creator: Yi Ouyang, Wei Wei, Zheng Xu

item.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
item.description: arXiv:2610.21511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $\beta$ of $L(s,\chi)$, for a primitive real character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,\chi)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $\beta$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Kimura

item.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.
item.dc:creator: Fateme Sajadi

item.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Lazda

item.title: A prime plus a square: A conditional 11/20 upper bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.21655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E_\square(N)$ count the positive integers at most $N$ that cannot be expressed as a prime plus a nonnegative integer square. Assuming that every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most $7/8$, we prove $E_\square(N)\ll_\eps N^{11/20+\eps}$ for every $\eps>0$. The proof combines a conductor-weighted mean-square estimate with a uniform estimate for certain families having a prescribed quadratic component. For these families, the large sieve depends on the varying part of the conductor, while an approximate functional equation controls the fourth moment using the full conductor. A zero-detection argument then absorbs all bands of zeros with real part at least $129/167$. The remaining bands and the minor arcs give the exponent $11/20$. The proof includes even denominators, completion and positivity of the singular series, and removal of proper prime powers.
item.dc:creator: J\'anos Pintz, Ingo Alth\"ofer

item.title: A New Bound for the Gauss Circle Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.21730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $E(X)=\#\{(a,b)\in\Z^2:a^2+b^2\le X\}-\pi X$. We prove that $E(X)=O_\varepsilon(X^{209/670+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, uniformly for real $X\ge4$. This breaks the $5/16$ threshold suggested by Huxley as a possible limit of the Bombieri--Iwaniec method at the time. The proof introduces two refinements: a cone distribution estimate that preserves separate fourth- and sixth-power contributions in the double large sieve, and an explicit inversion of Taylor-coefficient constraints that cancels the linear error in a pair-counting argument. These refinements, together with the Robert--Sargos and Watt spacing estimates and the Vinogradov mean value theorem, yield the improvement.
item.dc:creator: Xi Cen, Xitao Gao, Cheng Zhang, Junyong Zhang

item.title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $\Xi$-function
item.description: arXiv:2610.21800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $\Xi$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.
item.dc:creator: Diksha Rani Bansal

item.title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(\pi)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.
item.dc:creator: B\'eranger Seguin

item.title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
item.description: arXiv:2610.21899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrt\nu$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $\nu$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4; the second proof uses the two cited theorems as hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Ralf Stephan

item.title: A variation on local trilinear form
item.description: arXiv:2610.21920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Wang

item.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Davide Lombardo

item.title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2610.21952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2\pi} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2\pi}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( \mu(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.
item.dc:creator: Yochay Jerby

item.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
item.description: arXiv:2610.22000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.
item.dc:creator: Jingcheng Dong, S\'ebastien Palcoux, Arnaud Plessis

item.title: Ekedahl-Oort strata with a superspecial factor in unitary Shimura varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$ and let $O_K$ be an imaginary quadratic order in which $p$ is inert. For any $a,b\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ not both 0, denote by $M(a,b)$ the unitary Shimura variety that parametrizes principally polarized abelian varieties over $\mathbb{k}$ with an action of signature $(a,b)$ by $O_K$ (subject to certain compatibility conditions). For any $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, there is a natural product map $M(a,b) \times M(c,d) \to M(a+c,b+d)$, which induces a map on Ekedahl-Oort strata. In this paper we focus on product maps where at least one of the factors is superspecial, since most Ekedahl-Oort strata of unitary Shimura varieties contain such a factor. We describe maps with this property completely on the level of Weyl group coset representatives. We also characterize, on the level of Weyl group coset representatives, which Ekedahl-Oort strata of $M(a,b)$ admit a superspecial factor.
item.dc:creator: Emerald Andrews, Deewang Bhamidipati, Heidi Goodson, Steven R. Groen, Sandra Nair

item.title: Logarithmic exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a $1$-bounded multiplicative function, and suppose that $|\alpha-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$, where $(a,q)=1$ and $q\leq x$. We prove that $$ \left|\sum_{n\leq x}\frac{f(n)}{n}e( n\alpha)\right| \leq \left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}+o(1)\right)\frac{\log x}{\sqrt{q}}+O(\log q). $$ Here the constant $4/\sqrt{6}$ is optimal. This settles two conjectures of Granville and Lamzouri recently. If $f$ is completely multiplicative, the constant improves to $1$. The main new ingredient is a two-prime Ramar\'e decomposition identity.
item.dc:creator: Haozhe Gou

item.title: The discrete second moment of the Riemann zeta-function along powers of Gram points
item.description: arXiv:2610.22107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $t_k$ be the Gram points, and let $d\geq1$ be a fixed integer. Put $\eta_d=1/(2^{d+1}-2)$, $\sigma_d=1-\eta_d/d$, and $\sigma_d^*=7/8$ for $d=2$ and $\sigma_d^*=\sigma_d$ otherwise. We prove that, uniformly on compact subsets of $\sigma_d^*<\Re s<1$, $$ \frac1N\sum_{k=2}^{N}|\zeta(s+it_k^d)|^2 \longrightarrow \zeta(2\Re s). $$ The underlying result is a mean-square approximation by finite Euler products. For the squares of Gram points, grouping equal frequency ratios and applying the double large sieve improves the general derivative-test boundary $11/12$ to $7/8$. Assuming the Lindel\"of hypothesis, both the Euler-product approximation and the second-moment formula hold on every compact subset of $1/2<\Re s<1$, for every fixed $d\geq1$. As an application, we obtain a discrete universality theorem along the same Gram-power shifts, in the same unconditional and conditional regions.
item.dc:creator: Marius Dundulis, Ram\={u}nas Garunk\v{s}tis, Antanas Laurin\v{c}ikas, Raivydas \v{S}im\.{e}nas

item.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
item.description: arXiv:2610.22226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Da Ronche, Matteo Longo, Stefano Vigni, Francesco Zerman

item.title: Automorphic Dirac Operators and an Analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator on $\Gamma \backslash \mathfrak{H}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the 2010's Bombieri and Garrett showed that the discrete spectrum, if any, of a self-adjoint extension of a restriction of the hyperbolic Laplacian on the upper half plane is $s(s-1)$ where $\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}(i)}(s) = 0$. However, they also showed that at most 94% of the zeros of zeta can participate in this spectrum. In an effort to obtain a larger discrete spectrum, Sands in 2020 characterized an automorphic Hamiltonian that is an analogue of the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator for the modular curve. The motivation for this is that the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator is a discretized version of the Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}$. In describing this operator, it is necessary to understand automorphic Dirac operators and the growth of the potential. Here, we explain several noteworthy features of automorphic Dirac operators, prove that Sands' Hamiltonian has a purely discrete spectrum using an explicit presentation of Kronecker's limit formula, and use the operator to give a characterization of an automorphic Schwartz space.
item.dc:creator: Marcella Manivel

item.title: On exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\leq1}$ be multiplicative, and suppose that $\alpha$ has a rational approximation $a/q$ with $|\alpha-a/q|\leq 1/(qx)$ and $q\leq x/((\log x)^2(\log\log x)^3)$. We prove that $\left|\sum_{n\leq x}f(n)e(n\alpha)\right|\leq \left(\frac4{\sqrt6}+o(1)\right)\frac{x}{\sqrt q} +O\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$, whereas complete multiplicativity improves $4/\sqrt6$ to $1$. Both constants are optimal. In particular, this confirms a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients motivated by the work of Montgomery and Vaughan (1977). We also obtain logarithmically weighted estimates and give counterexamples to related conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Haozhe Gou

item.title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors
item.description: arXiv:2610.21051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Tommy Hofmann, John Nicholson

item.title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.21265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, the smallest number $\xi_n(m)$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices is $2(nm-S_3(m))$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. After rescaling, these numbers are the values at the points $m/3^n$ of a continuous function $T$ of Takagi type, the Delange function of base $3$. Both facts are known. In this paper, we study the local structure of $T$. The local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals, that is, the numbers $m/3^n$ with integers $m$ and $n\ge0$. The local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$, where $k$, $m$ and $n$ are integers with $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize the points $x$ where $T$ has an infinite derivative from one or both sides, in terms of their ternary digits $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$. At a ternary rational the derivative is $+\infty$ from the right and $-\infty$ from the left. At every other point, the derivative from the right is $+\infty$ exactly when the digit slopes $2\sum_{j\le n}(1-\xi_j)$ tend to $+\infty$. The derivative from the left is $+\infty$ exactly when a stronger condition holds, which also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of consecutive zeros among the digits $\xi_j$. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged, and twos replace zeros. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. For the finite cubes, we show that over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, the maximum of $\xi_n(m)$ exceeds the larger of its values at the two ends of the block by exactly $\max\{3^{k-|d|}-1,0\}$, where $d=n-k-s_3(a)$. Finally, the variation $V_n$ of $T$ over the partition of $[0,1]$ into the $3^n$ intervals $[m/3^n,(m+1)/3^n]$ satisfies $V_n/\sqrt n\to4/\sqrt{3\pi}$, and we compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Chengyi Zhu

item.title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.21559v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By B\'ezivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.
item.dc:creator: Nha Xuan Truong

item.title: Generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
item.description: arXiv:2610.21577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with exponent $\exp(G)$. For positive integer $k$, the generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant, denoted by $\mathsf s_{k\exp(G)}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of length at least $\ell$ over $G$ has a zero-sum subsequence of length $k\exp(G)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any $n\ge 1$, \[\mathsf s_{3\cdot 2^n}(C_{2^n}^3)=6\cdot 2^n-3 \quad\text{and}\quad \mathsf s_{4\cdot 3^n}(C_{3^n}^3)=7\cdot 3^n-3. \] This completes all the remaining cases in the study of $\mathsf s_{kq}(C_q^3)$, where $q$ is a prime power and $k\ge 3$. As a consequence, for every $k\ge 3$, we have \[ \mathsf s_{kn}(C_n^3)=(k+3)n+O(\frac{n}{\log n}). \] This verifies a conjecture of Kubertin asymptotically. Our approach combines the previous group ring techniques and a recent powerful generalization of the Chevalley-Warning and Ax-Katz theorems introduced by Grynkiewicz
item.dc:creator: Hanbin Zhang, Shiwen Zhang

item.title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $\Phi(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{\Phi,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.
item.dc:creator: Josef Dick, Friedrich Pillichshammer

item.title: B\'ezout bounds and rational points on quasianalytic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For functions $f : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $\mathcal C_M$, we establish explicit bounds for the number of intersection points of the graph $\Gamma(f)$ with algebraic curves of degree at most $d$. The bounds are given in terms of the Bang degree determined by the weight sequence $M$, the degree $d$, and the norming constant of $\Gamma(f)$ with respect to the space of real bivariate polynomials of degree at most $d$. We give instances, where the bounds are at most polynomial in $d$ and, consequently, the graph $\Gamma(f)$ contains few rational points: the number of rational points of height at most $H$ is bounded by a polynomial in $\log H$.
item.dc:creator: Armin Rainer

item.title: An undecidable problem in dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a variety $X$ with a self-map $\phi$ and subvarieties $Y$ and $Z$ of $X$, we consider the set of $n$ for which $\phi^n(Y)$ intersects $Z$ nontrivially. Extending a beautiful construction of Lee and Nam, we show this gives rise to an undecidable problem for a fixed ambient variety $X$ and morphism $\phi$. We further use this construction to give a counterexample to a conjecture of the author, Satriano, and Sierra.
item.dc:creator: Jason Bell

item.title: Unimodular Zeros of Selmer's Harmonic Trinomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.22132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $n>k$ be positive integers and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}$. In this note, we classify the unimodular zeros of the harmonic trinomial $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}$ given by \[ H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(z)=z^n+\varepsilon\overline z^{\,k}+\delta, \] where $\overline{z}$ is the complex conjugate of $z\in \mathbb{C}$. Let $g:=\gcd(n,k)$ be the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $k$, and set $n_0:=n/g$ and $k_0:=k/g$. For each choice of $\varepsilon,\delta\in \{-1,1\}$, we give a necessary and sufficient congruence involving $n_0$ and $k_0$ to guarantee that $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ has unimodular zeros. More precisely, if the corresponding congruence holds, then $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ has exactly $2g$ unimodular zeros, which are given explicitly; otherwise, it has no unimodular zeros. The proof uses a reduction to a trinomial equation and elementary divisibility arguments.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Barrera, Waldemar Barrera, Juan Pablo Navarrete

item.title: Double covers of tori for p=2 and genuine functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In his work on $L$-embeddings and double covers of tori over local fields, Kaletha associates to a maximal torus $S$ in a connected reductive group a canonical double cover $S(F)_{\pm}$ and introduces a genuine sign function $a_S$ associated to a genuine character of $S(F)_{\pm}$. We give two constructions of this genuine sign function over a non-archimedean local field, including residual characteristic $2$. The first uses rootwise lifts to the double cover; the second, in characteristic zero, uses the exponential map. Under explicit ramification conditions, both constructions yield genuine sign functions which, in odd residual characteristic, agree with his construction. We also illustrate the case of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$. A brief announcement of the first construction appears in Appendix D of that work.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Gratien, Nhat Hoang Le, Kazuki Tokimoto

item.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=n^2$ with small $x_3$, revisited
item.description: arXiv:2211.00412v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $r(N)$ be the number of representations of $N$ as a sum of two squares. For every integer $n\ge 2$ we prove an asymptotic formula for $\sum_{x\equiv e \bmod 2}\Phi(x/M)\,r(n^2+x^2)$, that is, for the number of integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=n^2$ with $x_3\equiv e \bmod 2$ in a range $|x_3|\ll M$, with smooth weight $\Phi$. The formula has an explicit secondary term and a power saving in the error term, and it is non-trivial as soon as $M\ge n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$, that is, $M\ge D^{1/2-1/12+\varepsilon}$ with $D=n^2$. The leading term is $\frac{4}{\pi}(\log n)\int\Phi(x/M)\,dx$, independently of the arithmetic of $n$; this corrects the main term stated in the published version (Ramanujan J. 63 (2024), 293-337). The proof factorises $n+ix_3$ in $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, which leads to Kloosterman sums. These are estimated by Weil's bound, combined with a Plancherel argument that exploits the curvature of the underlying quadric. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: Rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree
item.description: arXiv:2505.00680v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $N$ be a positive integer and $X_0(N)^*$ be the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(N)$ by its full group of Atkin-Lehner involutions. Elkies conjectures that the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ are only cusps or CM points when $N$ is large enough. We establish an integrality result for the $j$-invariants of non-cuspidal rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree, representing a significant step toward resolving a key subcase of Elkies' conjecture. To this end, we prove the existence of rank-zero quotients of certain modular Jacobians $J_0(pq)$. Furthermore, in the non-squarefree case we provide a complete classification of the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ of genus $1 \leq g \leq 5$, when they are finite. In the process we identify exceptional rational points on $X_0(75)^*$ and $X_0(147)^*$ which were not known before.
item.dc:creator: Sachi Hashimoto, Timo Keller, Samuel Le Fourn

item.title: Breaking Universality in the Lower Order Terms in the 1-level and 2-level Density of Holomorphic Cusp Newforms
item.description: arXiv:2508.21691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Katz--Sarnak density conjecture predicts that the normalized low-lying zeros of a family of $L$-functions ordered by analytic conductor $R$ converge, as $R \to \infty$, to the eigenvalue statistics near $1$ of a classical compact group, and that the limit depends on the family only through its symmetry type. We study the first correction to this limit for families of holomorphic cusp newforms of fixed weight $k$ and varying level $N$. Sharpening work of Miller on lower order terms in the one-level density, we evaluate the harmonically weighted one- and two-level densities with errors $O\left(\log^{-5}(R)\right)$ and $O\left(\log^{-2}(R)\right)$, and show that each of them already differs at order $\log^{-1}(R)$ from an explicit universal profile built out of $k$, the test functions, and $R$ alone. We compute that difference exactly. It is the product of a functional of the test functions with a single arithmetic invariant $\kappa_1(F)$ of the family, an explicit sum over the bounded prime factors of the level. Two families of newforms of the same weight and the same symmetry type, with conductors of the same size, therefore have densities whose first lower order terms differ by an explicit nonzero amount whenever their levels have different bounded prime factors.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Amit, Lucas Chen, Lawrence Dillon, Christopher Housholder, Xiaoyao Huang, Joshua Khan, Say-Yeon Kwon, Meiling Laurence, Steven J. Miller, Vishal Muthuvel, Devayani Pradhan, Luke Rowen, Pramana Saldin, Connor Yau, Steven Zanetti

item.title: Counting rational points on non-uniruled surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.07060v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be a non-degenerate non-uniruled irreducible projective surface of degree $d$ defined over a number field $K$, and let $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)$ be the number of rational points of $X$ of height at most $B$ that do not lie on lines contained in $X$. Assuming a suitable hypothesis on the size of the rank of Abelian varieties, we show that $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,n,d,\varepsilon}B^{\frac{n+1}{n}+\varepsilon}$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, if $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^3$ is a smooth projective surface of degree $d\ge 4$ defined over a number field $K$, then $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,d,\varepsilon} B^{4/3+\varepsilon}$. This conditionally improves a bound of Salberger for $d=4$ and $d=5$. The proof, based on an argument of Heath-Brown, consists of cutting $X$ by projective hyperplanes and using a uniform version of Faltings's Theorem, due to Dimitrov, Gao, and Habegger, to bound the number of rational points on the hyperplane sections of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Andreaus

item.title: Computing bounded solutions to linear Diophantine equations with the sum of divisors
item.description: arXiv:2601.17832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an efficient computational method for finding all solutions $n\leq U$ to the Diophantine equation $a\sigma(n)=bn+c$, where $a,b,c$ are fixed integer coefficients, $U$ is a given upper bound, and $\sigma(n)$ denotes the sum of divisors of $n$. The method combines advanced pruning of possible prime factors of $n$ and their combinations with several optimization techniques, organized around a \emph{prime-wheel} data structure developed for this purpose. It is implemented in the {\sc SageMath} computer algebra system within the framework of recursively enumerated sets and supports native {\sc MapReduce} parallelization. We apply the method to numerous previously studied equations, discovering new solutions, certifying complete solution lists below substantially larger bounds than previously reported, and substantially improving lower bounds in several open problems involving the sum-of-divisors function.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: A Ceiling Continued Fraction Approach to the Erd\H{o}s-Straus Conjecture: Heuristic finiteness of counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2605.04551v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the Ceiling Continued Fractions (FCT) framework for constructing three-term Egyptian fraction representations in the Erd\H{o}s--Straus conjecture from divisors of the shifted integers \(p+i\). A probabilistic model for their arithmetic structure leads to an asymptotic upper-bound heuristic for cumulative failure. The resulting bound is summable, and the first Borel--Cantelli lemma assigns probability zero to the event that infinitely many primes survive the full FCT block. Computational tests on \(10^9\) Mordell-type primes at each of the scales \(10^{17}\), \(10^{52}\), and \(10^{131}\) found no counterexamples.
item.dc:creator: Andres Ventas

item.title: Arcsine kernels, inverse-binomial harmonic sums, and classical hypergeometric transformations
item.description: arXiv:2607.09904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study inverse-central-binomial series with finite reciprocal-square factors and harmonic weights involving $H_n$, $H_{2n}$, and $1/n$. An arcsine integral gives explicit odd-zeta evaluations and a classification of coefficientwise cancellation within a polynomial ansatz. The scalar examples include an evaluation of weight seven and a direct proof of Sun's Conjecture 3.10. An entire generating relation organizes a second family with finite rational coefficient formulas. We then derive that relation, a supplementary generating family, and the complete two-order construction from Bailey's cubic transformation, contiguity, Gauss's quadratic and connection formulas, Euler's transformation, and Clausen's identity. The derivation retains all three infinity branches and resolves the vanishing denominators in the lower contiguous value. A doubling relation with a unique analytic solution and an explicit algebraic identity complete the proof. Thus the evaluations have a proved classical origin; no independent new hypergeometric summation principle is claimed. An application of a known complete-monotonicity property gives strict signs and global Taylor bounds. All endpoint limits, parameter derivatives, and coefficient extractions are justified.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: The Richelot isogeny graph and paramodular forms of weight 3: Atkin-Lehner signs and certified spectra
item.description: arXiv:2608.14145v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Richelot $(2,2)$-isogeny graph $G_p$ of superspecial abelian surfaces in characteristic $p$ is the genus-2 analogue of the supersingular isogeny graph: its weighted adjacency matrix is a Brandt matrix for a compact inner form of $\mathrm{GSp}_4$, and it commutes with an Atkin-Lehner involution $R(\pi)$. Refining Ibukiyama's conjectures, we conjecture the automorphic origin and the $R(\pi)$-sign of every eigenvalue: Eisenstein, Saito-Kurokawa, Yoshida and paramodular eigenvalues, and pairs of type-Va eigensystems that only $R(\pi)$ separates. We compute $G_p$ at 33 primes, with up to 2176 vertices, and certify the predicted eigenvalues and signs in exact arithmetic; at $p=167$ and $173$, where the sign prediction first becomes non-trivial, the graph carries the predicted eigenvalue $-8$ with sign $-1$. For every prime we prove that each type-Va parameter contributes exactly one eigenline of each $R(\pi)$-sign, a closed formula for the trace of $R(\pi)$, and a Fricke sign bias. If no further CAP representations occur, the non-trivial spectrum lies in $[-8\sqrt{2}, 6+4\sqrt{2}]$, both ends being sharp under the conjecture, and only Saito-Kurokawa eigenvalues exceed $8\sqrt{2}$; at all 104 primes $p\le 601$ the extreme eigenvalue computed by Florit and Smith agrees with the largest Saito-Kurokawa one. Finally, the irrational roots of the residual square factor form one Galois orbit with full symmetric Galois group at each certified prime $p\ge 29$, and the spectrum appears to follow a Plancherel law.
item.dc:creator: Hung T. Dang

item.title: Tight universality of $m$-gonal forms with minimal criterion sets
item.description: arXiv:2609.12779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For integers $m\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, an $m$-gonal form is called tight $\mathcal{T}(n)$-universal if it represents exactly the positive integers $\mathcal{T}(n)=\{ n, n+1, n+2, \ldots \}$. In this paper, we study the minimal criterion set $\mathrm{CS}(m,n)$ for tight $\mathcal{T}(n)$-universality. Our main result determines $\mathrm{CS}(m,n)$ for all $n \geq8$, $3 \leq m \leq \left\lfloor \frac{3n+1}{2} \right\rfloor$. More precisely, \[ \mathrm{CS}(m,n)= \begin{cases} \{ n, n+1, \ldots, 2n-1 \}, & m=5,\newline \{ n, n+1, \ldots, 2n \}, & m\neq5. \end{cases} \] We also establish the corresponding tight $\mathcal{T}(n)$-universality results and show that the upper bound on $m$ is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Byeong Moon Kim, Ji Young Kim

item.title: Non-Archimedean Poincar\'e series and geodesics on the Bruhat-Tits tree
item.description: arXiv:2609.23964v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adapting a construction of Kurihara in the setting of Drinfeld modular forms, we define Poincar\'e series on the Drinfeld half-plane $\Omega$. These series are built from products of meromorphic $1$-forms that are naturally associated to geodesics on the Bruhat-Tits tree. We establish convergence under a finiteness condition on the geodesics, verify this condition in several cases, and give sufficient conditions for the resulting cusp forms to be nonzero. For the principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(\mathfrak{n})$ of $GL_2(\mathbb{F}_q[T])$, we construct explicit linearly independent families of Poincar\'e series by lifting certain $k$-forms from the components of the analytic reduction of $\Gamma(\mathfrak{n})\backslash\Omega$. We formulate conjectures on the vanishing orders at cusps, and we prove the first of them for an explicit family of Poincar\'e series by computing the corresponding expansions at the cusps; as an application, we obtain the Drinfeld modular forms $h$ and $\Delta$ as Poincar\'e series (up to a sign). Finally, for cocompact groups attached to quaternion algebras over $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$ that split at $\infty$, we show that the Poincar\'e series span the whole space of modular forms of given weight and type.
item.dc:creator: Milan Berger-Guesneau, Mihran Papikian

item.title: Farey Symbols for the Picard Group
item.description: arXiv:2609.36629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop Picard Farey symbols for finite-index subgroups of \(G=\PSL_2(\ZZ[i])\) from the Gaussian Farey tessellation of \(\HH^3\) by ideal octahedra. The ambient geometry naturally involves two different index-two extensions of \(G\): the orientation-preserving group \(\PGL_2(\ZZ[i])\) and a reflection extension. This distinction explains the two \(G\)-orbits of Farey faces, which merge into one \(\PGL_2\)-orbit, and the classical extended modular tessellation appears as a totally geodesic slice. A Picard Farey symbol records finitely many Gaussian-rational octahedral occurrences, their local stabilizers, and cooriented face-pairing transformations. We prove that such a symbol reconstructs the finite Picard-cell action and hence the subgroup; moreover, when subgroup membership is decidable, the symbol can be found by a terminating finite double-coset procedure. For torsion-free subgroups we obtain whole-octahedron fundamental domains. The marked symbol also supplies finite orbit relations for the established Gaussian Steinberg edge--face presentation, with its corresponding Bianchi modular-symbol relations. When the natural modular-to-Picard coset map is bijective, a side-connected Kulkarni special polygon lifts, using the same modular representatives, to a Picard fundamental polyhedron whose intersection with the invariant real plane is exactly that polygon; the level-$(2+i)$/level-$5$ family is worked out explicitly. Comparison examples show that octahedral boundary minimization, absolute geometric face minimization, and preservation of such a modular section are distinct problems. Canonical reduction and effective Hecke reduction remain open.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari, Helena Verrill

item.title: The linear independence of $1$, $\zeta(3)$, and $\zeta(4)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.06838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent breakthrough, Fauzan proved the irrationality of $\zeta(5)$. In this paper, we combine Fauzan's determinant method with classical simultaneous approximations of zeta values studied by Zudilin and Dauguet--Zudilin to prove the linear independence of $1$, $\zeta(3)$, and $\zeta(4)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. As a corollary, $\zeta(3)/\pi^4$ is irrational.
item.dc:creator: Li Lai

item.title: Amplified moments and a refinement of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.15291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a uniform $7/8$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, together with its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions. Assuming the analytic inputs of that work, we improve the boundary from $7/8=0.875$ to $8748867/10000000=0.8748867$ for the same families. The improvement combines a relaxed direct estimate with an amplified first moment of the reflected numerator, obtained from the existing fourth-moment estimate. A two-stage parameter argument yields the stated boundary without strengthening the inverse-moment estimate.
item.dc:creator: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang

item.title: Zero density in short strips and short-interval bounds toward Hypothesis S
item.description: arXiv:2610.15989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We deduce zero-density estimates in short vertical strips from short-interval moments of globally tempered automorphic $L$-functions, by adapting the large-value estimate of Guth and Maynard and the Type II zero argument of Maynard and Pratt to the framework of Ye and Zhang. For the Riemann zeta function, we obtain $N_\zeta(\sigma;T,T+T^a)\ll T^{15a(1-\sigma)/(3+5\sigma)+\varepsilon}$ for $2/3\le a\le1$ and $7/10\le\sigma\le4/5$, improving Ye--Zhang's exponent in the interior of this range. Combining the localized density bound with the recent quasi-Riemann theorems, we estimate smoothed prime-power sums with phase $\exp(2\pi i\alpha n^\beta)$ on intervals of length $K^\delta$. For $0<\beta<13/20$, we obtain a power saving whenever $\max\{17/30,1-\beta\}<\delta<1$; in particular the square-root phase admits every $\delta>17/30$. A revised transform estimate retains both the stationary spread and the Fourier width $K/L$. For example, the bound at $\beta=1/2$, $\delta=3/5$ is $K^{15/26+\varepsilon}$, uniformly for frequencies $m\alpha$ with $1\le m\le K^{1/10}$. We also retain power savings for certain self-dual $GL(2)$ twists and self-dual $GL(3)$ cusp forms, without assuming Ramanujan. All three applications have explicit frequency dependence.
item.dc:creator: Yangbo Ye

item.title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.16751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound for automorphism groups of algebraic function fields in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic function fields in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. In this article, we firstly investigate solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ where $p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$, \[ |G|\le C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}(g_F-1), \qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1). \] In particular, one may take $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article , we give asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\mathbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\operatorname{Aut}(F_i/\mathbb{F}_q)$, such that \[ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1). \] For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian curve gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the asymptotic lower bound of Ma and Xing \cite{MaXing2019} for subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ whose order is relatively prime to $p$. As another application, we extend our method for bounding solvable automorphism groups to $p$-solvable subgroups, obtaining explicit linear bounds in terms of the genus.
item.dc:creator: Henning Stichtenoth, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

item.title: A new way integral for the $n$-fold cover of $SL_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.19110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\pi$ be a genuine irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of the $n$-fold cover $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ of $SL_2(\mathbb{A})$, $n \geq 3$ odd, and let $\tau$ be the genuine representation of $GL_1^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ obtained from a unitary Hecke character of $\mathbb{A}^\times$. We prove that, for a certain choice of data, a new way integral for $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ represents the partial $L$-function $L^S(ns+\tfrac12,\pi\times\tau)$. The integral is derived from the generalized doubling integral of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan, following the idea of Ginzburg and Soudry.
item.dc:creator: Tianxiang Liu

item.title: Fppf-descent for condensed animated rings
item.description: arXiv:2311.13408v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we define "animated affinoid algebras" and prove some basic properties of them. Then we generalize the result of the previous paper of the author and the result of Lucas Mann (fppf-descent for discrete rings or affinoid algebras) to discrete animated rings or animated affinoid algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yutaro Mikami

item.title: Kernels of Arithmetic Jet Spaces and Frobenius Morphism
item.description: arXiv:2601.22591v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$, the Frobenius morphism between arithmetic jet spaces restricts to generalized kernels of the projection map. Using the functorial properties of such kernels of arithmetic jet spaces, we show that this morphism is indeed induced by a natural ring map between shifted $\pi$-typical Witt vectors. In the special case when $G = \hat{\mathbb{G}}_a$, the arithmetic jet space, as well as the generalized kernels are affine $\pi$-formal planes with Witt vector addition as the group law. In that case the above morphism is the multiplication by $\pi$ map on Witt vector schemes. In fact, the system of arithmetic jet spaces and generalized kernels of any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$ along with their maps and identitites satisfied among them are a generalization of the case of the Witt vector scheme with the system of maps such as the Frobenius, Verschiebung and multiplication by $\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Kumar Mishra, Arnab Saha

item.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
item.description: arXiv:2604.06979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Demarche

item.title: Jacobi Endpoint Pencils and Sharp Interlacing for Centered Binomial Samples
item.description: arXiv:2608.08714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study interlacing between real polynomial quotients obtained from centered binomial samples of a fixed even or odd real entire function at consecutive odd degrees. For sources of order at most one, we determine the optimal vertical-strip half-widths guaranteeing weak interlacing for every adjacent pair: $\sqrt{15/28}$ for even sources and the explicit algebraic constant $h_*\approx 1.0656$ for odd sources. These constants are forced by the first nontrivial pair and suffice at every degree. Under the same sharp bounds, nonpolynomial sources have simple zeros in $(-2,2)$ and strict interlacing at every positive index. We also prove an eventual result: if a nonpolynomial source has growth order less than two and only finitely many zeros off the imaginary axis, then all sufficiently high adjacent quotients have simple interior zeros and strictly interlace; the starting index depends only on the finite factor formed from those zeros. The proof turns the sampling problem into an interval real-rootedness problem for a Jacobi differential operator. For fixed degree, we also determine the maximal range of scalar shifts preserving real-rooted polynomials with at most one zero outside the interval. Applications give strict interlacing for quotients attached to completed Dedekind zeta derivatives and to successive centered blocks of critical values of self-dual newforms satisfying explicit spacing and parity conditions.
item.dc:creator: Seokho Jin

item.title: Edit distance exponents for irrational rotations
item.description: arXiv:2608.11763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study quantitative edit-distance asymptotics for symbolic codings of irrational rotations $x \mapsto x+\alpha$ on $\mathbb{T}$ in terms of the irrationality exponent $\mu(\alpha)$. For the binary coding determined by an interval $[0,\beta)$, let $d_N(x,y)$ be the edit distance between the codings of the orbits of the points $x$ and $y$ up to time $N-1$. For every $\alpha \notin \mathbb{Q}$, almost every $\beta \in (0,1)$, and almost every $x,y \in \mathbb{T}$, we determine the edit-distance exponents $\displaystyle (*) \; \; \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \frac{\rho(\alpha)}{\rho(\alpha)+1} \; \;$ and $\; \; \displaystyle\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \min\Bigl\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{\rho(\alpha)}\Bigr\}$, where $ \rho(\alpha):=\mu(\alpha) - 1$. We find a surprising transition at the golden mean $\varphi= \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$: If $ \rho(\alpha) \le \varphi$, then both asymptotics in $(*)$ hold for all $\beta$. However, for every finite $\rho>\varphi$, there is an uncountable set of $\alpha$ with $\rho(\alpha)=\rho$ for which both edit-distance exponents are strictly smaller than the corresponding values in $(*)$ for uncountably many $\beta$. We also derive consequences for aperiodic circle homeomorphisms and Sturmian sequences. For rotations of $\mathbb{T}^d$ coded by boxes, we prove that for almost every rotation vector, the common edit-distance exponent is $d/(d+1)$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Best, Yuval Peres

item.title: Disproof of a Conjectured Upper Bound for the Davenport Constant
item.description: arXiv:2609.29878v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G= C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ be a finite abelian group with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$, and let $\rr(G)=r$ denote its rank. The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of $\ell$ elements of $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, and $\DD^*(G)=1+\sum_{i=1}^r(n_i-1)$ is its classical lower bound. A long-standing conjecture asserts that $\DD(G)\le\DD^*(G)+\rr(G)-1$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture. More strongly, we prove that $\sup_{\rr(G)=r}\bigl(\DD(G)-\DD^*(G)\bigr)=\infty$ for every fixed $r\ge5$. Thus the classical lower bound does not approximate the Davenport constant within an additive error depending only on the rank. More precisely, our construction gives $\delta(C_m^{r-4}\oplus C_{3m}^3\oplus C_{6m})\ge m$ for all integers $r\ge5$ and $m\ge2$. Consequently, the least rank $r_0$ for unbounded Davenport excess $\DD(G)-\DD^*(G)$ satisfies $3\le r_0\le5$. Our result also disproves the Narkiewicz--\'{S}liwa conjecture of 1982 \cite{NS82} on the Narkiewicz constant, arising in algebraic number theory from the quantitative study of algebraic integers with unique factorization. The same amplification of the Davenport excess yields counterexamples to Girard's conjecture \cite[Conjecture 1.2]{Girard08} on the cross numbers of long zero-sum-free sequences. As a further main result, we establish the uniform upper bound $$\DD(G)\le\frac{16}{5}\rr(G)\exp(G)$$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. The classical estimate of van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk \cite{vEBK69} gives $\DD(G)\le\exp(G)\left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \le\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$. Our bound removes the logarithmic factor $\log\exp(G)$ from this classical estimate, and replaces it with the absolute constant $16/5$.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang
